title: Set up your wallet
description: Create a wallet and go straight to receiving and sending. Winnow starts encrypted iCloud backup automatically when available.
journey: Create a wallet without a recovery-word checklist.
Reach the wallet home screen and see its backup status.
limitations: Without iCloud the wallet still works and shows Not backed up. Save a manual backup; recovery words and backup controls are in Advanced. The recorded simulator journey does not validate live iCloud.

title: Receive bitcoin
description: Label who an address is for, or what the payment is for, before sharing it. You can skip. Matching payments carry the local note in your wallet.
journey: Tap Receive and skip the optional address label.
Read the receive address and return to the wallet; fund the address from the test node and mine a block.
Check the funded balance and the received payment in wallet history.
limitations: An address label does not verify the sender or create a payment destination. Labels are included in encrypted iCloud recovery, but not in manual wallet files.

title: Send bitcoin
description: Choose an account, recipient, and amount. Check the address, fee, and total before sending or continuing to the account’s approvals.
journey: Open Send in beginner mode, paste an address, and enter the amount.
Review the destination, amount, and fee before sending.
Check that Bitcoin Core accepts the payment; mine a block, see the receipt confirm, and return to wallet history.

title: Pay someone again
description: Name someone you’ve paid, or save their payment card. Next time, choose them in Send.
journey: Open a sent payment and save its recipient with a name.
Next time, choose the saved person in Send. A payment card can provide a fresh address for each payment.

title: Name who paid you
description: Give a received payment a local name without attaching an address. Add a payment card or explicitly choose a destination before sending.
journey: Open a received payment and save a local name for its sender.
Add a payment card or choose a destination explicitly before using Send to that person.
limitations: Funding addresses are unverified destinations, not proof of who paid you. Winnow never selects one automatically. Sending to an address again can reveal address reuse.

title: Choose a funding destination
description: If you choose to consult an explorer, review what is disclosed before asking. Then explicitly select any returned destination.
journey: Open the funding-address lookup and review the transaction ID and what the explorer learns before giving consent.
Choose a returned address explicitly, even if the explorer returns only one.
Save the destination with its unverified origin visible.
limitations: The explorer receives the transaction ID and your connection's IP address. Returned addresses do not identify people.

title: Save with other people
description: Choose who shares the wallet and how many approvals a payment needs. With two approvals out of three, one person can be away and the other two can still pay.
journey: Receive test bitcoin into a script-path 2-of-3 account containing the phone’s key and two Bitcoin Core cosigners.
Review a payment, approve on the phone, and add one Core cosigner’s approval; the other Core key is available but unused.
Send and check that the node accepts the payment and the app discovers its confirmation.
limitations: For shared control, each person must keep their own key. If you choose just one required approval, any one of them can spend.

title: Combine your phone with another signer
description: Use 2-of-2 MuSig2 so your phone and a separate key must both approve every payment. You can also use a MuSig2 group as one cosigner in a larger threshold vault.
journey: Receive test bitcoin into a 2-of-2 MuSig2 account shared by the phone and one Bitcoin Core cosigner.
Review a payment and exchange signing data between the phone and Core; both keys are required.
Send and check node acceptance and confirmation in the app.
limitations: This journey uses Bitcoin Core as the second signer. It does not establish hardware-wallet compatibility or every signing order. Keep the wallet backup file, the phone’s recovery words, and a separate backup of the other signer’s key. Every key is required.

title: Back up and restore
description: Automatic encrypted iCloud backup restores this phone’s signing key, history, shared accounts, saved people and labels. Manual files remain available.
journey: Create a wallet; backup begins without an Enable step. A successful save appears only after iCloud acknowledges it.
On a replacement device, Winnow discovers backups automatically. Select one and authenticate; automatic updates resume using a separate record.
Use Advanced for recovery words, manual exports or disabling cloud backup. Without iCloud, keep a combined manual history-and-key file for spending recovery.
limitations: Automatic updates wait for pending payments to confirm. Cloud and Keychain synchronization can be delayed. Other owners’ signing keys are not included. Older cloud copies may lack names and labels.

title: One screen, or the full set of controls
description: Beginner mode is one screen with no settings. Advanced mode, one tap from its corner, is the three-tab interface: fee controls, network connections, signing tools and every setting.
journey: Create, receive, and send using the beginner interface.
Return to the one-screen wallet and see its balance and payment history.

title: Inspect and import signing policies
description: Create a Taproot vault from public signer keys and coordinate approvals using PSBT text. Inspect the policy and reviewed transaction explicitly.
journey: Use the phone-plus-Core MuSig2 account and the script-path 2-of-3 account within the same wallet journey.
Receive into each account, review a payment, collect its required approvals, and confirm the spend.

title: Replace a pending payment with a higher fee
description: Review a replacement’s fee and change before authorizing it. The original remains visible as replaced.
journey: Open a pending outgoing payment in Advanced mode and choose Bump fee.
Review the replacement’s fee and change before authorizing it. History keeps the original marked as replaced.

title: Inspect peers and control external disclosure
description: Inspect connected peers and network settings. Explorer links open only after an explicit warning about the information sent to that website.
journey: Open Advanced settings to inspect connected peers.
Review the warning before opening an external explorer; cancel to stay in the app.
Use Reset and shuffle peers when you want to discard remembered candidates and reconnect.
limitations: Explorer websites are not wallet backends. A single or coordinated set of peers can still withhold information; multiple connections are not proof of independent operators.

title: Refresh the peer list
description: Download dated candidates from Winnow’s census without interrupting active peers. Reset and shuffle peers is a separate action.
journey: Choose Refresh peer list in Advanced settings, then read the observation date and candidate counts.
Existing connections stay active while the new list becomes available for future connections.
Reset and shuffle remains a separate choice.
limitations: Downloads expire after seven days; saved peers and DNS discovery remain available. Downloaded census entries count as one trust source. Every selected peer still undergoes normal wallet checks.
